Hello David,

You can uninstall on OS X using the following commands. http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/documents/rro/installation/#revorinst-uninstall

To uninstall Revolution R Open on OS X:

Run the following command to uninstall:
   cd /Applications
   sudo rm -rf "Revolution R Open".app
   cd /Library/Frameworks
   sudo rm -rf R.framework   sudo rm /usr/bin/R
   sudo rm /usr/bin/Rscript

Note: You cannot run CRAN R and Revolution R Open 8.0 side by side on OS X at this time.

Regards,

Hi David,
I have Revolution R Open installed side by side with CRAN R on my Macbook Pro.

I installed CRAN R via the popular Homebrew <http://brew.sh/> package manager:
brew update ; brew tap homebrew/science ; brew install R
Per default, brew will install the latest stable R release to /usr/local/bin/R.

I also have my system paths set to reference /usr/local/bin before /usr/bin.

RRO will create a /usr/bin/R (it's actually a symlink) that RStudio will pick up without any manual intervention. Though I am not familiar with Rcmdr, I see no Reason why it would have an issue with RRO.

To summarize:
I have RRO and CRAN R on my system at the same time. In the terminal I can call either one I want. In my GUI applications, they will automatically reference RRO, which is at /usr/bin/R.

Hope this helps you out,

-Chris Mosetick

messages.subject: Re: RRO Beginner
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Simon

Welcome to the forum and thank you for trying RRO.

RRO is 100% R with some additions.

Possibly the most visible of these is the inclusion of the Intel Math Kernel Libraries.  This math engine gives you the benefit of higher performance for all functions using matrix math, due to implicit parallelisation across multiple cores of these calculations.  The great thing is you don't have to make a single change to your code to benefit from this.  See my blog post at http://blog.revolutionanalytics.com/2014/10/revolution-r-open-mkl.html for more details.

The Revobase package mainly contains some functions to interact with the MKL, e.g. setting the number of threads to use.  You can view the package help by typing

    library(help=Revobase)

into the R console.

So as not to interfere with any other R installations on your machine, the package library is in a different location - you can find this with .libPaths().  This means you start with a clean slate, as you discovered.  We are considering some options for easier migration between releases and versions and might include this in future.

I hope this helps.

Andrie

messages.body_plain:
Hi Scott,

The code snippet provided above by David C. correctly explains how you would retrieve your task results when working with the Background task runtime. What follows here is more general advice on working with the framework and also a recommendation.

Your initial intuition to look for your task output variables, plots, console, etc. in the RTaskResult was absolutely correct. In most cases, those data would indeed be available on the RTaskResult. However, when working with the Background task runtime specifically, things work a little bit differently. This is because the Background task runtime is intended to be used when you anticipate long-running tasks that you would like to schedule for execution now and then have your application collect the results at some future date, perhaps hours or days later.

Based on the description you provided of your own use case it sounds like you want to execute your tasks and collect the results immediately. If that is the case, then the Background task runtime is probably not the right choice. You should consider using the Discrete task runtime or if maximizing throughput is very important to you, perhaps the Pooled task runtime. Using either the Discrete or Pooled task runtime your task results will be directly available to your application in your RTaskResults.

If you haven't had a chance to do so, I recommend checking out the RBroker Framework tutorial <http://deployr.revolutionanalytics.com/documents/dev/rbroker/>. It provides a step-by-step introduction to the framework. Importantly, the RBroker Runtime Options section <http://deployr.revolutionanalytics.com/documents/dev/rbroker/#runtimes> discusses the suitability of each supported runtime which is definitely worth looking over. At the end of the day, choosing the right runtime is key to getting the most from the framework, while keeping things simple in your application code.

David R

Hi, Danilo

Thank you for trying RRO and I'm glad you like it.

I tried your code in a Ubuntu 14.04 virtual machine and both packages installed without a problem, using the code you provided.

It seems unlikely to be the cause of your problem, but I had to install some Linux system dependencies first. Specifically, devtools requires RCurl, and RCurl depends on the linux libcurl-dev library.

To install this, I used the following in Linux:

sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install libcurl4-openssl-dev

Then devtools installed without a problem and my github packages installed.

It's a shot in the dark, but let me know what you find.

Regards

Andrie
